meta.name: QuartzOS Reference Data
meta.description: Production-grade reference data for cannabis concentrate dabbing — banger form factors, concentrates, sensors, and a parameterized metrology calibration model. v2.0.0 replaces the fused single-offset calibration with the research-derived four-term equation: T_IR_Setpoint = T_Ideal + dT_Load + dT_Gradient + dT_emissivity. Sourced from manufacturer documentation (Dab Rite, Highly Educated, Quave, Honeybee Herb), brand guidance (710 Labs, Mood, Press Club), thermophysical properties of fused silica, and 2025-2026 community consensus.
meta.license: Open data for non-commercial integration. Verify temperature recommendations against current community testing before production deployment.
meta.temperature_convention: Two distinct temperature anchors are tracked per concentrate: (1) surface_temp_optimal_f — the INTERIOR QUARTZ SURFACE temperature at the moment of dab introduction (probe-truth, what a Terpometer V1 contact probe reads). (2) fluid_target_optimal_f — the target BOILING TEMPERATURE of the concentrate fluid itself (what determines vapor production and terpene preservation). Surface > fluid by the phase-change load constant (~65°F) which the surface must supply to the cold extract mass on contact.

model_breakdown.dT_Load: calibration.constants.phase_change_load_f — cold-mass + cap heat-sink deficit (sample-mass dependent)
model_breakdown.dT_Gradient_total: banger.gradient_lag_f × wall.gradient_multiplier — transient conduction lag from interior to exterior surface (Fourier's law over wall thickness)
model_breakdown.dT_emissivity: sensor.emissivity_bias_f × banger.emissivity_bias_multiplier — radiometric calculation error from sensor firmware emissivity vs. material true emissivity

data_sources: Dab Rite official documentation and 2025 placement guide (dabrite.com)
420 VapeZone empirical Dab Rite + slurper testing
Press Club temple ball / hash temp guidance
Reddit r/Dabs, r/QuartzBangers, r/COents technique threads (2024-2026)
Thermophysical properties of fused silica (k=1.4 W/m·K, ρ=2200 kg/m³, Cp=730 J/kg·K, ε≈0.92 at 400-600°F)
Stefan-Boltzmann radiometric analysis of Dab Rite Pro v2.2 firmware (ε_set=0.95)
migration_notes_v1_to_v2: REMOVED: banger.ir_offset_f and banger.ir_offset_sign (fused single-offset model)
ADDED: banger.gradient_lag_f — Fourier's-law conduction lag for the banger's measurement geometry
ADDED: banger.emissivity_bias_multiplier — modifies sensor emissivity bias for opaque vs. clear quartz
ADDED: concentrate.fluid_target_optimal_f and fluid_target_range_f — the boiling target before phase-change load
ADDED: sensor.emissivity_bias_f — firmware-vs-material emissivity calculation error (per sensor)
ADDED: wall.gradient_multiplier — wall thickness scales gradient lag (Fourier τ = L²/α)
ADDED: calibration.constants — phase_change_load_f, fused_silica thermal properties
PRESERVED: surface_temp_optimal_f and surface_temp_range_f (probe-truth, contact sensors use directly)
PRESERVED: wall.modifier_f (legacy field — soft additive override on top of gradient_multiplier)

fields.gradient_lag_f: dT_Gradient component of the metrology equation: signed °F. Positive = exterior measurement face is COOLER than dab interface (bucket-class during cooldown). Negative = measurement face is HOTTER than dab interface. Zero = measurement face IS the dab interface (e-nail). Anchored at standard wall (3-4mm); wall.gradient_multiplier scales for thinner/thicker.

explanation: 1. T_Ideal := concentrate.fluid_target_optimal_f (the boiling target of the oil itself)
2. dT_Load := calibration.constants.phase_change_load_f (sensible + latent heat absorbed by the cold extract mass and cap on contact, ~65°F for a 0.1-0.2g dab)
3. dT_Gradient := banger.gradient_lag_f × wall.gradient_multiplier (Fourier's-law conduction lag from interior to the exterior face the IR sensor sees)

4. dT_emissivity := sensor.emissivity_bias_f × banger.emissivity_bias_multiplier (firmware ε_set=0.95 vs. quartz ε_actual≈0.92 produces ~15°F under-reading on Dab Rite for clear quartz; the Opaque Quartz preset cancels most of this for opaque bottoms)
5. For contact probes (Terpometer V1): dT_Gradient and dT_emissivity collapse to 0; setpoint = surface_temp_optimal_f (probe reads interior directly).
6. For e-nail PID: setpoint = surface_temp_optimal_f + sensor.emissivity_bias_f (PID coil-vs-surface offset, NOT radiometric).

constants.phase_change_load_note: Instantaneous interior-surface temperature drop when a 0.1-0.2g cold (70°F) extract mass is introduced and a cold carb cap is seated. Sum of sensible heat (raise oil to boiling point) + latent heat of vaporization + conductive loss to cap. Tolerance ±15°F per dab volume.

fused_silica.note: Constants used to derive gradient_lag_f via Fourier diffusion time τ = L²/α.

workflow_notes.ir_descent_dab: Dab Rite alarms when temp DESCENDS through the set point. Torch past the displayed target, pull the flame, dab when the alarm fires on the way down. Don't dab AT peak torch.
workflow_notes.contact_probe_vs_ir: If you have a Terpometer V1 contact probe AND a Dab Rite, they will show different numbers for the same dab — and both are correct. The probe reads interior surface; the IR reads exterior wall thermal radiation through firmware-assumed emissivity. The new model explicitly accounts for this via the dT_Gradient and dT_emissivity terms.
workflow_notes.opaque_quartz_preset: The Dab Rite Pro v2.2 'Opaque Quartz' emissivity preset largely cancels the ε bias for nucleated/sandblasted bottoms — but does NOT cancel the gradient lag, which is actually LARGER for opaque (air pockets restrict thermal conduction).
